response.sql: WITH cat AS (SELECT category, AVG(remaining) AS avg_remaining, SUM(amount - spent) AS total FROM budget WHERE amount > 75 GROUP BY category), overall AS (SELECT AVG(total) AS avg_total FROM cat) SELECT cat.category, cat.avg_remaining, cat.total, cat.total - overall.avg_total AS above_overall_avg FROM cat, overall WHERE overall.avg_total IS NOT NULL AND cat.total > overall.avg_total;

assumptions.assumption: "Passes the 75-dollar cutoff" means amount is strictly greater than 75 (amount > 75). Budget lines with amount exactly 75 are excluded.

Missing values are handled by SQL aggregate semantics: AVG(remaining) and SUM(amount - spent) skip rows where the value is NULL, and a category with no non-null values returns NULL (blank). The overall average skips categories whose total is NULL, and the final filter returns no rows when that average is NULL.
Budget rows with a NULL category form their own group, as GROUP BY treats NULL as a single group.

alternatives.interpretation: The cutoff is inclusive: budget lines whose amount is at least 75 (amount >= 75) are kept.
